### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s).

**18** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 12b9daf7493f30ebb5faf47e7b40eb99d2bda267`.

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **28** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 12b9daf7493f30ebb5faf47e7b40eb99d2bda267` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3643828353f5d12fa446f582de26a434c9eca1c2` — the merge of head `a6ae742c8934a66e220149e2f6effc0d890e4185` into base `12b9daf7493f30ebb5faf47e7b40eb99d2bda267`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3643828353f5d12fa446f582de26a434c9eca1c2 && git checkout 3643828353f5d12fa446f582de26a434c9eca1c2
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 12b9daf7493f30ebb5faf47e7b40eb99d2bda267 a6ae742c8934a66e220149e2f6effc0d890e4185 && git checkout -B drift-repro 12b9daf7493f30ebb5faf47e7b40eb99d2bda267 && git merge --no-ff a6ae742c8934a66e220149e2f6effc0d890e4185

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 12b9daf7493f30ebb5faf47e7b40eb99d2bda267
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 12b9daf7493f30ebb5faf47e7b40eb99d2bda267` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `11d4d8c6ee1ba9b802108064670d1362e5ce87bb`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #22839 (body and all three comments: triage 6109249693, claim 6109361423, os-dev-report 6109800087), PR #22849 (body, five-file list, net diff against `main`), the check-runs on the head (polled last at 2026-10-11T14:10:08Z), and `origin/main` (`d48931871`) for `packages/cli/src/commands/compile.ts`, `packages/cli/src/utils/lower-callables.ts`, `packages/cli/package.json`, `src/index.ts`, `src/hook-body.ts`, `src/console.ts`, the `--json` consumers under `packages`, `scripts`, `.github/workflows`, `packages/qa`, `content/docs`, `docs/qa`, and the changeset gates.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept set of `objectstack build --strict-body` — a narrowing only; the code is right, the changeset's scoping of it is not (② item 4).** Traced on the diff against the walk at `origin/main`: every registered ref ends in `loweredRefs` (some slot extracted it) or in `unlowered` (refused, an authored-`body` slot, or a `functions` entry), and `bodylessCallables` is `unlowered` minus `loweredRefs`. The old gate refused iff a warning existed or `count − bodyExtracted` exceeded 0. Refuse → pass cannot happen: a refused ref is never in `loweredRefs` (`extractHookBody` is a function of the handler's source alone; `originLabel` only words the message), and `count` above `bodyExtracted` leaves at least one ref outside `loweredRefs`, which is then a row. Pass → refuse happens exactly when no refusal exists and a never-tried callable is masked by a callable extracted more than once (`bodyExtracted` counts per slot, `count` per ref). Two reachable shapes: (a) the same callable at the top level and in a `packages[i].manifest` body (the PR's probe H, the changeset's third BREAKING bullet); (b) one function object bound as the handler of two or more bodyless hooks or actions in ONE walk, beside a `functions` entry or an authored-`body` slot — a handler shared by two objects plus a `functions` entry is ordinary authoring. For (b) the old arithmetic read count 2, bodyExtracted 2, no warning, so the gate passed (and, by the same arithmetic, `needsBundle` emitted no bundle, so the `functions` entry shipped with no implementation — the #22853 family, single-walk member); the new list carries one row naming the `functions` entry, so the build is refused, correctly. On every refusal the exit code (1) and the `error` string (`strict-body: missing body`) are byte-identical to before; the header's wording is unchanged and its number drops by the placeholder row (and by the duplicates on a double-walked stack). Verdict on the direction question: narrowing only — right.

2. **`bodylessCallables` population — right.** It is exactly "each registered callable that no slot lowered into a body, once": `unlowered` is a Map keyed by ref and `noteUnlowered` keeps the first row, the filter drops every ref some slot lowered, and the order is registration order for every surviving row (a surviving ref was lowered nowhere, so its first slot both registered and noted it). A refused handler's row is the extractor's warning object itself (identity pinned in the unit file). The authored-`body`-beside-inline-function case belongs in the list: the old gate already refused it (`count` exceeds `bodyExtracted` by one for it), `needsBundle` (`stillNeeded` above 0) emits the runtime module for it and the bundle carries every registered ref, and the flag's stated purpose in `compile.ts` is to enforce body-only before bundle emission goes mandatory-off. The rejected definition ("a slot runs it from the runtime module") would have moved that stack refuse → pass while `--no-runtime-bundle` kept refusing it: a widening, and the dev was right to refuse it. Both reason constants state true facts about where the callable runs.

3. **Public surface — internal only; right.** `@objectstack/cli`'s `exports` map is `.`, `./console`, `./hook-body` and `./package.json`. `src/index.ts` re-exports command classes only; `src/hook-body.ts` re-exports `extractHookBody`, `HookBodyExtractionError` and two types from `extract-hook-body.ts`; `src/console.ts` re-exports console utilities. `lower-callables.ts` is unreachable from any published entry, so `bodylessCallables`, `BodylessCallable`, `FUNCTIONS_ENTRY_NO_BODY_REASON` and `AUTHORED_BODY_BESIDE_FUNCTION_REASON` widen no published surface. `LoweringResult` gains one required field, additive for every in-tree reader (`compile.ts`, `lint.ts`, `validate.ts`, `author-time-rules.ts`, `scaffold-validate.ts`, and `packages/qa/dogfood/test/build-shaped-artifact.ts`, which imports by workspace-relative path, its own comment recording that the deep `dist` import was retired); no in-tree literal constructs a `LoweringResult` (the only other mentions are two comments). The four Type Check runs are green on this head. The changeset's "no spec key, export, type or stored shape moves" holds for the published surface.

4. **`--json` `issues` shape — right.** The placeholder row leaves; a refused handler's row is unchanged (`origin`, `reason`, `kind`, `freeIdentifiers`); a never-tried callable gets `{ origin, reason }`, the shape the placeholder already had, so no key is new on the payload (`success`, `error`, `issues`, `warnings`, `conversions` as before). Consumers re-measured by me on `origin/main` `d48931871` (later than the dev's `1eff3224d`), same result: the aggregate placeholder origin and its reason text occur only at the producer (`compile.ts:340`); `strict-body: missing body` is read by `build-json-failure-warnings.e2e.test.ts:437` (`error` and `warnings`, not `issues`), anchored as source text by `truncation-remainder-notices.test.ts:411` (the anchor survives in the new `compile.ts`), captured by a manual step in `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/cli.json:1344` that reads no row, and quoted in `CHANGELOG.md`; every `payload.issues` read in the cli tests is on another exit; no `--strict-body` invocation exists in `.github/workflows`, `scripts` or `examples`. Removing the row outright with no summary field is the right call; the triage's "or a separate summary field if a consumer needs it" found no consumer.

5. **The rest of the Unchanged paragraph — right.** The `compile.ts` hunk is the `--strict-body` block alone. The walk's outputs (`lowered`, `functions`, `count`, `bodyExtracted`, `bodyExtractionWarnings`, `loweredHookRefs`) are untouched; only bookkeeping is added. The default build, its 2c warning lines, `bodyExtractionWarnings` in the success payload and `needsBundle` do not move. Every source-text anchor in `truncation-remainder-notices.test.ts` (the header template, the list `issues`, the `printBulletList` call with `limit: 20`, the `error: 'strict-body: missing body', issues,` payload line, the two 2c precedent lines) is present in the new file, so that pin needed no edit.

6. **Pins — each can fail; right.** Leg A (`compile.ts` back to warnings plus placeholder): the header reads 2 and 5 against the pinned 1 and 4, and the `with-function` case lists the hook then the aggregate placeholder origin instead of `function 'sbc_score'`; the control is a control and stays green by design. Leg B′ (list equals the raw warnings): the `functions`-entry cases, the authored-`body` case, the single-walk equality (3 rows pinned, 1 produced) and both ADR-0130 D4 cases (two rows for one refused hook; no row for the shared `functions` entry) go red. Leg C (the `loweredRefs` filter dropped): the hook-plus-`functions`-entry-sharing-one-function case produces a row where `[]` is pinned. The bullet regex matches `printBulletList`'s two-space-bullet format, the refusal kind `free-identifiers` and `freeIdentifiers: ['slugOf']` are what the extractor emits for a module-scope identifier, and both helpers (`defineStackSourceFromLiteral`, `linkSpec`, `childEnv`) exist on `main`. Tier: the new file spawns the CLI (child_process, `run-dev.js`, the tsx binary), so the behaviour predicate in `vitest-tiers.ts` puts it in the `integration` project, and its queue-tier name keeps it in the per-PR run; Test Core and all six shards are green on this head, so the door pins ran in CI. One gap, carried into ②: shape (b) of item 1 has no pin; the adjacent "lowered at ANY slot" case is the non-moving variant of it.

7. **Docs — right.** `hook-bodies.mdx:173` and `:345` remain true (the flag still fails on a refused body, exit 1, per-callable diagnostic); "Flag docs affected by code changes" is green.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset: `@objectstack/cli: minor`, conventional `!` summary, a BREAKING banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, one adr-0087 marker comment reading `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` with its why.
- **`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` — right.** Clause ② is a new key on a published payload (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs`'s own definition); this diff adds none, and the `{ origin, reason }` row shape pre-existed as the placeholder's. The arm is `(narrowing)` because the accept set narrows (① item 1) and the `issues` list narrows (the placeholder leaves). The triage's `Clause-②: yes` was a grade shape, not a ruling, and would have been wrong as a reading (nothing is added); the claim corrected it before dispatch and the PR's third acceptance note says why. Per AGENTS.md the `(narrowing)` arm IS breaking, so the `!` summary, the banner and the ADR-0087 marker are required and present; `minor` is the launch-window grade for a breaking change (`major` is refused by `check-changeset-no-major`). Consistent. "Check Changeset", the job that runs `check-empty-changeset`, `check-adr-0087-registration` and `check-changeset-no-major` on the merge base, is green on this head.
- **ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` — consistent.** No authorable key, published export or stored shape moves and no stored row is read or rewritten, so `objectstack migrate meta` has nothing to derive; the marker closes the other categories on facts (published package, no existing id, a build diagnostic rather than a runtime interface or type surface). The body's "one-line fix" sentence is a note for a script reading a CLI row, not a metadata FROM → TO prescription; the gate's detector did not read it as one and the gate is green.
- **The Unchanged paragraph's first sentence — WRONG, and this is the finding that decides the verdict.** It says: for a stack that is walked once, `--strict-body` refuses exactly the stacks it refused before. ① item 1 shape (b) is a stack walked once that moves from pass to refuse: one function object as the handler of two or more bodyless hooks or actions, beside a `functions` entry or an authored-`body` slot. The third BREAKING bullet attributes the masking to the `packages` double walk alone, so the moved set is under-described by one reachable shape, in the text that ships to consumers as `CHANGELOG.md`. The PR body's "every stack walked once gets exactly the verdict it got before: the old gate refused iff `count − bodyExtracted` exceeds 0, which is iff this list is non-empty" carries the same over-claim (the "iff" fails in that shape), and the probe table has no row for it. The `bodylessCallables` docblock in the diff already states the true condition ("only when every callable is walked once" — walked at one slot), so the fix is a wording alignment, not a code change. Remedy: (1) reword the Unchanged sentence to the docblock's condition (a stack in which each callable is bound at one slot), (2) add shape (b) to the third BREAKING bullet or as a fourth, and (3) one unit case pinning shape (b): old `count − bodyExtracted` equal to 0, new list of one row naming the `functions` entry. Nothing else in the changeset or the code needs to move.
- Everything else the changeset states (FROM → TO for the row and the header, the refusal's unchanged fields, exit code and `error` string, default build, warning lines, `bodyExtractionWarnings`, runtime-bundle decision) holds against the diff.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none declared; none found beyond ② item 4.
- Deviation "landing point in `lower-callables.ts`": covered by the claim's widened file surface (comment 6109361423) and right on the merits — the deduped population can only be built where refs are minted; `extract-hook-body.ts` is untouched, so PR #22834/#22837's hold is respected.
- Deviation "pins in two new files, not `truncation-remainder-notices.test.ts`": right; that file's anchors hold untouched (① item 5), and a door pin belongs in a spawning file, which the tier predicate then places correctly (① item 6).
- Deviations "heavy runs through the lock with nohup", "gate record carries the re-run exit": process notes with no contract effect; the derived gates' verdicts of record are the check-runs on the head.
- Deviation "commit trailers model-free per AGENTS.md": the repo rule governs; no contract effect.
- "Role file vs order: no conflict": accepted.
- `out_of_scope_findings[0]` (`needsBundle` reads `count − bodyExtracted`, so a double-walked stack with a `functions` entry ships no runtime module): filed separately as #22853; not this PR's scope, since fixing it changes which builds emit the bundle. Escalation for #22853's lane: ① item 1 shape (b) is the single-walk member of the same family (one shared handler object masks a `functions` entry in `needsBundle` too) and belongs on that card's shape list.
- `out_of_scope_findings[1]` (stale comment in `build-multi-package-artifact.e2e.test.ts` about what `composeStacks` preserve writes): comment-only, no contract effect; left to #22853's lane or a nit.
- Acceptance note 3 (triage `yes` versus claim `no (narrowing)`): ruled in ② — the PR's line stands.
- The seat's correction to the leg-A sentence in the PR body (first leg A run without `dist`, final re-run with `dist` built and still red): present in the PR body as the dev asked; consistent with "the child loads `src`".
- Check-runs on the head, latest run per name, at 2026-10-11T14:10:08Z: every run `completed` with `success` (Build Core, Test Core and its six shards, Dogfood Regression Gate and its three shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance, the four Type Check runs, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, the claim and single-writer guards, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected) or `skipped` (Auto Label, Check PR Size, Console Pin Gate, Build Docs, Packed-tarball smoke), except **`Lint & Repo Gates`, still `in_progress`** — read as pending, not green; it carries the repo-wide `pnpm lint` and `check:changeset-gate-self-tests`, and the dev's lint-narrowing argument covers only the four linted files. The FAIL below rests on ② item 4 and stands regardless of that run; the re-spin lands on a new head whose check-runs are read afresh.
- No maintainer ruling and no earlier record on this head exist on the card; this is the first record naming it.
